page: Microsoft Azure D48lds_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Dldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU is equipped with a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. System memory is configured at 96.0 GB, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes 2835 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage, but does not include integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong computational capabilities, particularly in single-threaded compression tasks. The server achieves top-tier performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.36 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.96 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 302.08 GB/sec, falling into the top 25%. Passmark CPU metrics are consistently strong, with an overall CPU score of 66237.87 and an encryption test score of 50504.51. For memory-bound operations, the system records a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 3537.72 GB/sec, while large-block uncached read and write bandwidths are 174.64 GB/sec and 69.06 GB/sec, respectively.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance represents a compute-heavy profile with a low memory footprint relative to its processing power. This resource density makes it cost-efficient for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory allocations, such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 75.8 GB/sec, and Redis key-value operations, processing 79.57 million SET operations per second. It also demonstrates strong efficiency in lightweight machine learning tasks, processing 338.79 tokens per second for text generation on a small 135M model. The primary tradeoff is the limited 96.0 GB of RAM for a 48-vCPU system, which may constrain large-scale in-memory databases. Appropriate workloads include web serving, cryptography, compression tasks, and database operations utilizing the local 2835 GB storage.
